### iliad-115 (17.673–761)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἀπέβη ξανθὸς Μενέλαος (17.673) | "So then, having spoken, went away fair-haired Menelaus" | "So he spoke, and fair-haired Menelaus went away" | follows the Odyssey table’s ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἀπέβη (Odyssey 4.657) and ξανθὸς Μενέλαος "fair-haired"; "departed", "strode away" |
| πάντοσε παπταίνων (17.674) | "everywhere glancing about" | "glancing about on every side" | per the table (13.649), unchanged |
| πόδας ταχὺς … πτώξ (17.676) | "the swift-in-feet cowering hare" | "the hare, swift of foot" | "fleet-footed", "swift-footed" (reserved for ποδώκης, ποδάρκης); ταχύς "swift" with πόδας as for πόδας ὠκύς; πτώξ is "hare" in `i` (+ note: the word is built on the idea of cowering), "cowering hare" in `l` |
| θάμνῳ ὑπ’ ἀμφικόμῳ (17.677) | "a bush with leaves all round" | "a thick-leaved bush" | "bushy", "tufted", "leafy" (ὑλήεις is "wooded"); ἀμφί "around" + κόμη "hair, foliage" |
| ἐξείλετο θυμόν (17.678) | "it took out its life" | "takes out his life" | the table’s ἐξείλετο θυμόν "had taken out his life" (15.460), unchanged; the aorist of the simile is turned to the present in `i` |
| ὄσσε φαεινώ … δινείσθην (17.679–680) | "your two eyes, shining … were whirled about" | "your two shining eyes turned in every direction" | "gleaming", "bright" (reserved for ἀργύφεος, λευκός); ὄσσε "eyes" (3.427), δινέω "whirl" (cf. δινεύω 4.541) |
| κατὰ ἔθνος … ἑταίρων (17.680) | "over the company of your many companions" | "over the company of your many companions" | "band", "troop"; follows the table’s ἔθνος ἑταίρων "company of his companions" (11.585, 17.581) |
| ἀμφασίη ἐπέων (17.695) | "speechlessness of words" | "speechlessness" | "silence", "dumbness", "bewilderment"; ἀ- negative + the root of "say"; rare noun |
| τὼ δέ οἱ ὄσσε δακρυόφι πλῆσθεν, θαλερὴ δέ οἱ ἔσχετο φωνή (17.696 = Odyssey, odyssey-020) | "and his two eyes were filled with tears, and his full voice was checked" | "and his eyes filled with tears, and his strong voice was choked" | the Odyssey’s English, with "her" changed to "his" because a man is speaking; no other change |
| ἐφημοσύνη (Μενελάου ἐφημοσύνης ἀμέλησε, 17.697) | "of Menelaus’ behest … was he neglectful" | "he did not neglect Menelaus’ behest" | "command", "order", "charge"; follows the published Odyssey rendering of ἐφημοσύνη as "behest" (odyssey-059; odyssey-080, "the whole behest"), rare noun; ἐπιτέλλω keeps "lay charge on" (17.668) |
| ἀμελέω (17.697) | "was neglectful of" | "did not neglect" | "ignored", "disobeyed", "forgot"; ἀ- negative + μέλει |
| βῆ δὲ θέειν (17.698) | "went to run" | "set off running" | the table’s βῆ δὲ θέειν (11.617), unchanged |
| ἀμύμονι ἑταίρῳ (17.698) | "a blameless companion" | "his blameless companion" | "noble", "faultless"; the table’s ἀμύμων "blameless" |
| δάκρυ χέοντα (17.700) | "a tear shedding" | "shedding tears" | the table’s δάκρυ χέων, unchanged |
| πόδες φέρον ἐκ πολέμοιο (17.700) | "his feet carried out of the war" | "his feet carried him … out of the war" | "ran" (the note says the feet are a way of saying he ran), "fighting" in `l` |
| κακὸν ἔπος ἀγγελέοντα (17.701) | "an evil word about to tell" (the table’s "to tell the news", with the object already given by ἔπος) | "to tell him an evil word" | "bad news" (ἀγγελίη is "news"), "message"; follows ἀγγελέουσα "to tell the news" / "to bring news" (8.398, 8.409) |
| οὐδ’ ἤθελε θυμὸς … τειρομένοις ἑτάροισιν ἀμυνέμεν (17.702–703) | "Nor … was the heart willing to defend the worn-down companions" | "Nor was your heart … willing to defend the worn-down companions" | "ward off for", "ward off ruin from" (`i` must not supply "ruin"), "help", "save"; the table’s ἀμύνω with the dative of a person and no thing warded off is "defend" (13.464, 13.481; 9.601); θυμός "heart" |
| τειρομένοις ἑτάροισιν (17.703) | "the worn-down companions" | "the worn-down companions" | "hard-pressed", "distressed", "exhausted"; follows τείρω "worn down" (5.352, 5.391) |
| μεγάλη δὲ ποθὴ Πυλίοισιν ἐτύχθη · … Δαναοῖσι τέτυκται (17.704, 17.690) | "a great lack for the Pylians was made" · "a great lack for the Danaans has been made" | "the Pylians were left with a great lack" · "a great lack has come upon the Danaans" | "longing", "grief", "regret", "loss"; follows ποθή "lack" (1.240) and ξενίων ποθή "lack of hospitality" (Odyssey 15.514); τεύχω "make" in `l` |
| διοτρεφές (vocative, 17.679, 17.685, 17.702) | "Zeus-nurtured one" | "Zeus-nurtured one" | "Zeus-nurtured" alone, "Zeus-nurtured Menelaus"; the table’s διοτρεφές "Zeus-nurtured one" (10.266, 11.819) |
| ὀΐομαι … γιγνώσκειν (17.687) | "I think" | "I think" | "I suspect" (the table’s 1.558 row; the shipped Iliad rows 10.551, 11.609, 11.834, 12.66 and 13.747 have "I think" for ὀΐω with an infinitive) |
| πῆμα … κυλίνδει (17.688) | "a woe a god is rolling" | "a god is rolling woe upon the Danaans" | "ruin", "bane", "trouble"; follows πῆμα "woe" (3.160, 6.282, 9.229); κυλίνδω "roll" (17.525, προπροκυλινδόμενος) |
| πέφαται … ὤριστος Ἀχαιῶν (17.689–690) | "has been killed the best of the Achaeans" | "the best of the Achaeans … has been killed" | "has been slain" (kept for ἐναίρω), "has fallen"; ὤριστος is ὁ ἄριστος (crasis) |
| ἀλλὰ σύ γ’ αἶψ’ Ἀχιλῆϊ θέων … εἰπεῖν (17.691–692, infinitive as command) | "But you, quickly, to Achilles, running … tell" | "But you, run quickly to Achilles … and tell him" | "I ask you to", "you must" (the infinitive stands as an imperative; the note says so) |
| γυμνόν (νέκυν … γυμνόν, 17.693) | "naked" | "naked as it is" | "stripped", "unarmoured" (the note says the armour is meant) |
| κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ (17.693) | "Hector of the glancing helmet" | "Hector of the glancing helmet" | the table’s κορυθαίολος, unchanged |
| κατέστυγε μῦθον ἀκούσας (17.694) | "was horror-struck, having heard the word" | "was appalled to hear what he said" | "hated", "shuddered" (στυγέω "hate" in `i` elsewhere), "was struck dumb"; καταστυγέω "be struck with horror" |
| Πηλεΐδῃ Ἀχιλῆϊ (17.701) | "Peleus’-son Achilles" | "Peleus’ son Achilles" | "Achilles, son of Peleus"; follows iliad-001 |
| Θρασυμήδεα δῖον ἀνῆκεν (17.705) | "Thrasymedes, heavenly, sent up" | "sent heavenly Thrasymedes" | "dispatched", "released"; ἀνίημι "send up" (cf. 6.256, "urged") |
| βεβήκει (ἐπὶ Πατρόκλῳ ἥρωϊ βεβήκει, 17.706) | "had gone" | "went back to stand over" | "had stepped", "was walking" (the note says the pluperfect stands for "was standing"); ἥρως "the hero" |
| εἶθαρ προσηύδα (17.707) | "at once spoke to them" | "at once spoke to them" | "straight away" (iliad-030 only), "addressed", "immediately", "forthwith"; the published iliad-075 (12.351, στῆ δὲ παρ’ Αἰάντεσσι κιών, εἶθαρ δὲ προσηύδα) has "and at once spoke to them", and iliad-069, -081, -109, -111 have "at once" for εἶθαρ |
| ἐπιπροέηκα (νηυσὶν ἐπιπροέηκα θοῇσιν, 17.708) | "I have sent forth, to the swift ships" | "I have sent him off to the swift ships" | "dispatched", "bidden"; follows προίημι "send forth" (11.796) |
| πόδας ταχύν (Ἀχιλῆα πόδας ταχύν, 17.709) | "swift in feet" | "swift of foot" | "fleet-footed", "swift-footed" (reserved for ποδώκης, ποδάρκης); the table’s πόδας ὠκύς, same rendering for ταχύς |
| οὐδέ μιν οἴω νῦν ἰέναι (17.709–710) | "and not him, I think, now to go" | "and I do not think he will go now" | "I suspect" (the table’s 1.558 row; the shipped Iliad rows 10.551, 11.609, 12.66 and 13.747 have "I think"), "I believe", "I fear" |
| κεχολωμένον Ἕκτορι δίῳ (17.710) | "angered with heavenly Hector" | "angry … with heavenly Hector" | "incensed" (reserved for χώομαι), "enraged", "furious"; χολόω "anger" from χόλος "anger" |
| γυμνὸς ἐών (17.711) | "being naked" | "without his armour" | "unclothed", "defenceless"; the note says γυμνός means unarmed |
| θάνατον καὶ κῆρα φύγωμεν (17.714) | "death and the death-fate may escape" | "escape death and the spirit of death" | follows θάνατον καὶ κῆρα "death and the spirit of death" (Odyssey 16.169) |
| Τρώων ἐξ ἐνοπῆς (17.714) | "from the Trojans’ shouting" | "out of the Trojans’ shouting" | "din", "war-cry" (ἀϋτή), "clamour"; follows the table’s ἐνοπή "shouting" (3.2) |
| ἡμεῖς δ’ αὐτοί περ φραζώμεθα μῆτιν ἀρίστην (17.712) | "But we ourselves, let us plan the best cunning" | "But let us ourselves plan the best stroke of cunning" | the published iliad-114 wording of the neighbouring line (17.634, ἀλλ’ ἄγετ’ αὐτοί περ …); only "But we" for ἀλλ’ ἄγετ’ differs, and περ is left untranslated there as here |
| πάντα κατ’ αἶσαν ἔειπες (17.716) | "Everything in due measure you have said" | "You have said everything as was fitting" | "rightly", "fairly", "justly"; the table’s κατ’ αἶσαν "in due measure" (3.59), "as was fitting" (iliad-110, 17.205) |
| ἀγακλεές (vocative, 17.716) | "very famous" | "very famous" | "renowned" (reserved for ἀγακλυτός), "glorious" (reserved for φαίδιμος), "illustrious"; ἀγα- intensifier + κλέος |
| ὑποδύντε … ἀείραντες (17.717–718) | "getting under it … having lifted" | "getting under it … lift the corpse and carry it" | "stooping beneath", "taking up"; dual participle with plural one; ὑποδύω "get under" |
| ἐκ πόνου (17.718) | "out of the toil" | "out of the toil" | "from the labour", "from the fight" (the note says the fighting is meant); πόνος "toil" |
| νῶϊ μαχησόμεθα (17.719) | "we two will fight" | "we two will fight" | "the two of us"; νῶϊ "we two", the dual |
| ἶσον θυμὸν ἔχοντες ὁμώνυμοι (17.720) | "having an equal heart, of the same name" | "of one equal spirit and bearing one name" | "namesakes" alone, "of one mind", "equal in courage"; θυμός "heart" in `l` |
| οἳ τὸ πάρος περ μίμνομεν ὀξὺν Ἄρηα (17.720–721) | "we who even before have stood against sharp Ares" | "we who even before this have stood against keen battle" | the table’s ὀξὺν Ἄρηα "sharp Ares" / "keen battle" (2.440, 4.352), unchanged; μίμνω "wait for, stand against" |
| ἀγκάζοντο (17.722) | "took up in their arms" | "gathered … up in their arms" | "embraced", "clasped"; ἀγκάζομαι from ἀγκάς "in the arms" (5.371) |
| ὕψι μάλα μεγάλως (17.723) | "very high, mightily" | "very high, with a mighty heave" | "greatly", "with great effort", "grandly" (each makes μεγάλως a moral word) |
| ἐπὶ δ’ ἴαχε λαὸς … Τρωϊκός (17.723–724) | "cried out loudly behind them the people of the Trojans" | "behind them the Trojan host raised a loud cry" | "shouted" (kept for ἄϋσε), "roared"; follows ἴαχε "cried out loudly" (4.125); λαός "people" in `l`, "host" in `i` |
| ὡς εἴδοντο (17.724) | "when they saw" | "when they saw" | "when they caught sight of"; εἴδοντο from the middle of the verb "see" |
| ἴθυσαν (17.725) | "charged straight" | "charged straight on" | "rushed", "darted" (kept for ἀΐσσω and ἀΐξω, 17.725–726); follows ἰθύει "charges straight on" (11.552) |
| κάπρῳ βλημένῳ (17.725–726) | "a boar struck" | "a struck boar" | "wounded boar", "hit boar"; follows κάπρος "boar" (Odyssey 11.131); βάλλω "strike" |
| κούρων θηρητήρων (17.726) | "young hunters" | "the young hunters" | "youthful", "strong"; κοῦρος "young man" (3.82), θηρητήρ "hunter" (5.51) |
| διαρραῖσαι (17.727) | "to tear apart" | "to tear it apart" | "to rend", "to break up", "to rip"; διαρραίω "shatter, tear apart" (the published iliad-012 has "shatter" and iliad-070 "raze" for a wall and a town; the tearing sense suits dogs and a boar) |
| ἀλκὶ πεποιθώς (17.728) | "trusting in its might" | "trusting in its strength" | "courage", "valour"; follows the table’s ἀλκὶ πεποιθώς "trusting in his might" (5.299), with "strength" in `i` |
| ἄψ τ’ ἀνεχώρησαν διά τ’ ἔτρεσαν ἄλλυδις ἄλλος (17.729) | "back they draw away, and in fright scatter, one this way, one that" | "draw back and scatter in fright, one this way and one that" | "fled", "trembled" (kept for the other ἔτρεσαν rows); follows ἄλλυδις ἄλλος "one this way, one that" (11.486, 11.745) and τρέω "took fright" (15.586) |
| εἷος μέν … ὁμιλαδόν (17.730) | "for as long as in a throng" | "for as long as they kept following in a throng" | "until", "while"; follows ἕως "until" for the conjunction; ὁμιλαδόν "in a throng" (12.3) |
| νύσσοντες ξίφεσίν τε καὶ ἔγχεσιν ἀμφιγύοισιν (17.731) | "stabbing with swords and with double-pointed spears" | "stabbed with swords and double-pointed spears" | the published iliad-078 wording; "two-edged"; νύσσω "stab" (11.565) |
| μεταστρεφθέντε … σταίησαν (17.732–733) | "having turned about … stood" | "turned round to face them and stood their ground" | "turned back", "wheeled" (kept for ἐλελίζω); optative of repeated action turned to "whenever" in `i` |
| τράπετο χρώς (17.733) | "the skin turned" | "the colour in the Trojans’ skin changed" | "turned pale", "went white" (the note says the colour left the skin), "flesh" (σάρξ); χρώς "skin" (4.510) |
| οὐδέ τις ἔτλη … δηριάασθαι (17.733–734) | "nor did anyone bring himself … to fight" | "no one could bring himself to … go on fighting" | "dared" (reserved for θαρσέω), "endured"; follows the table’s οὐδέ τις ἔτλη "no one could bring himself" (7.151) and δηριάασθαι "go on fighting" (16.96) |
| ἐμμεμαῶτε (17.735, 17.746) | "eager" | "full of eagerness" | "keen", "bent on it"; dual of μεμαώς "eager" (1.590) |
| πτόλεμος (17.736) | "war" | "the war" | "battle" (for μάχη); πτόλεμος is the older spelling of πόλεμος |
| ἐπὶ … τέτατο (17.736) | "was stretched upon" | "was stretched out over them" | "hung over", "raged"; follows τανύω "stretch" (11.336) |
| ἄγριος ἠΰτε πῦρ (17.737) | "savage like fire" | "savage as fire" | "wild", "fierce"; follows ἄγριος "savage" (4.23; Odyssey 7.206) and ἠΰτε "like" (1.359) |
| φλεγέθει · μινύθουσι (17.738) | "blazes" · "dwindle away" | "blazes" · "dwindle away" | "burns", "shrivel", "are consumed"; follows μινύθει "dwindle away" (16.392) |
| ἐν σέλαϊ μεγάλῳ (17.739) | "in a great blaze" | "in a great blaze" | "flash", "glare"; follows σέλας "blaze" (8.509) |
| ἐπιβρέμει ἲς ἀνέμοιο (17.739) | "upon it roars the force of the wind" | "the force of the wind roars upon it" | "blast", "might" (reserved for μένος), "strength" (σθένος); follows ἲς "force" (11.668) |
| ἀζηχὴς ὀρυμαγδός (17.741) | "incessant din" | "an incessant din" | "unceasing", "tumult"; the published iliad-091 (15.25) has the adjective ἀζηχής as "incessant pain", from the table’s ἀζηχές "incessantly" (4.435); ὀρυμαγδός "din" (2.810) |
| ἵππων τε καὶ ἀνδρῶν αἰχμητάων (17.740) | "of horses and of men, spearmen" | "of horses and of spearmen" | "warriors"; αἰχμητής "spearman" (17.588) |
| κρατερὸν μένος ἀμφιβαλόντες (17.742) | "strong might having cast about them" | "have cast strong might about themselves" | "put on", "gathered", "taken"; μένος "might" (2.387), ἀμφιβάλλω "throw around" |
| ἀταρπόν (17.743) | "footpath" | "footpath" | "path" (taken by οὐδός), "track", "trail"; follows ἀταρπιτός "footpath" (Odyssey 17.234), the same word |
| δοκὸν … δόρυ μέγα νήϊον (17.744) | "a beam … a great ship’s timber" | "a beam … a great timber for a ship" | "spear" (the note says wood, not weapon), "mast", "plank"; δόρυ "wood, timber" |
| καμάτῳ τε καὶ ἱδρῷ (17.745) | "weariness and sweat" | "weariness and sweat" | "toil", "labour"; follows κάματος "weariness" (4.230, 13.711; Odyssey 10.363) and ἱδρώς "sweat" (4.27); the published iliad-112 has "toil and sweat" for καμάτῳ δὲ καὶ ἱδρῷ (17.385), left as published |
| ἰσχανέτην · ἰσχάνει · ἴσχει (17.747, 17.750) | "held back" · "holds back" · "checks" | same | "restrained", "stopped", "holds back" for ἴσχει; ἰσχανέτην and ἰσχάνει follow ἰσχανάω "hold back" (5.89), and ἴσχει follows the table’s ἴσχει "check" (5.90) |
| πρών (ὥς τε πρὼν ἰσχάνει ὕδωρ ὑλήεις, 17.747) | "spur" | "wooded spur" | "headland", "ridge", "hill"; follows the table’s πρών "spur" (12.281) |
| πεδίοιο διαπρύσιον τετυχηκώς (17.748) | "right across the plain having come to be" | "a spur lying right across the plain" (+ note: the sense of τετυχηκώς is not certain) | "stretched", "built", "happening to be"; each decides the uncertain word |
| ἰφθίμων ποταμῶν ἀλεγεινὰ ῥέεθρα (17.749) | "of mighty rivers the grievous streams" | "the grievous streams of mighty rivers" | "strong", "violent", "painful"; follows ἴφθιμος "mighty" (1.3), ἀλεγεινός "grievous" (2.787), ῥέεθρα "streams" (2.461) |
| ῥόον πεδίον δὲ τίθησι πλάζων (17.750–751) | "the current to the plain it turns, making it stray" | "turns the current … out over the plain, making them stray" | "sends", "drives", "leads"; τίθημι "set" with the direction in -δε |
| ῥηγνῦσι σθένεϊ (17.751) | "do they break with strength" | "they do not break it with their strength" | "burst", "shatter", "force"; ῥήγνυμι "break", σθένος "strength" |
| μάχην ἀνέεργον ὀπίσσω Τρώων (17.752–753) | "held back the battle behind of the Trojans" | "held back the Trojan fighting from behind" | "pushed back", "turned away", "stopped"; follows ἀνέεργε "held back" (3.77) |
| Αἰνείας τ’ Ἀγχισιάδης (17.754) | "Aeneas, Anchises’-son" | "Aeneas, son of Anchises" | "Anchises’ son" in `l` only; the patronymic as for the other names |
| φαίδιμος Ἕκτωρ (17.754) | "glorious Hector" | "glorious Hector" | the table’s φαίδιμος, unchanged (4.505) |
| ψαρῶν νέφος · κολοιῶν (17.755) | "a cloud of starlings … of jackdaws" | "a cloud of starlings or of jackdaws" | "sparrows", "crows", "rooks"; follows the table’s ψῆρες "starlings" and κολοιοί "jackdaws" (16.582–583) |
| οὖλον κεκλήγοντες (17.756, 17.759) | "ruinously shrieking" | "shrieking ruinously" (+ note: sense of οὖλον here not certain) | "wildly", "in a swarm", "with deadly cries"; follows οὖλος "ruinous" (1.2), κεκλήγων "shrieking" (5.591) |
| προΐδωσιν (17.756) | "see beforehand" | "catch sight of" | "perceive", "spy"; πρό "before" + ἰδεῖν |
| κίρκος · φόνον φέρει (17.757) | "a falcon" · "slaughter brings" | "a falcon" · "brings slaughter" | "hawk" (ἴρηξ), "death", "murder" (kept for φόνος in the sense of killing a person); follows the Odyssey table’s κίρκος "falcon" (Odyssey 15.526) and φόνος "slaughter" (Odyssey 16.379, "steep slaughter") |
| σμικρῇσι ὀρνίθεσσιν (17.757) | "small birds" | "small birds" | "little", "weak"; σμικρός is the older form of μικρός |
| κοῦροι Ἀχαιῶν (17.758) | "the young men of the Achaeans" | "the young men of the Achaeans" | "sons" (reserved for υἷες), "youths"; the table’s κοῦροι Ἀχαιῶν (3.82) |
| λήθοντο … χάρμης (17.759) | "forgot the joy of battle" | "forgot the joy of battle" | "forgot their courage"; the table’s χάρμη "the joy of battle" (4.222) |
| πολλὰ τεύχεα καλά (17.760) | "many arms, fine" | "much fine armour" | "beautiful", "splendid"; follows τεύχεα "armour" (2.808), καλά "fine" |
| περί τ’ ἀμφί τε τάφρον (17.760) | "around and about the ditch" | "round and about the ditch" | "trench" (kept for the Odyssey 21.120 τάφρος), "moat"; follows τάφρον "ditch" (7.440, 7.449) |
